recommendation: Keep the audit as-is. Do not revive ObservationReliability in core unless OO opens and approves a new current-version tracker for a quality or signal-quality modeling requirement.
issue_request: FHIR-3002 asked about adding presumptive and confirmed microbiology concepts to ObservationReliability, but its final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution changed the DSTU1 Observation.reliability cardinality to 0..1, revised the reliability note, and clarified the unknown code definition.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-3002. Historical source contained the Observation.reliability / ObservationReliability machinery, and later commit 54f14f427c for FHIR-7154 made the reliability element inactive in the Observation spreadsheet source; #8479 then removed residual ObservationReliability binding-row source during Observation binding cleanup.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini actively includes Observation, and current source/observation/structuredefinition-Observation.xml defines Observation.status, Observation.dataAbsentReason, and Observation.interpretation with no Observation.reliability element. Source search found only source/bindings.ini and an old QUICK Library model-definition example mentioning ObservationReliability, which are not the authoritative current Observation element/value-set source. FHIR-7154, the later reliability-removal issue, is already represented on the combined branch by commit 315435578a61418aea568e0409ef16a6972fd47a.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is appropriate because reintroducing Observation.reliability, adding presumptive/confirmed codes, or editing stale non-authoritative matches would conflict with the later published removal of the element.
